title: Bridging finance facilitates lease extension on St John’s Wood flat
summary:
A property investor has secured £1,462,500 in bridging finance from SDKA to purchase a three-bedroom apartment in St John's Wood, using the loan term to pursue a Section 42 lease extension. The strategy aims to reduce ground rent and expand refinancing options with buy-to-let lenders.

title: Industry conference attendance remains low among estate agents
summary:
Estate agents in the UK show limited attendance at industry conferences despite professional development opportunities. Three primary barriers emerge: perceived relevance of speakers, time constraints, and cost considerations, with ticket prices ranging from free to approximately £500.

title: Wimbledon development secures £3m exit finance
summary:
Shawbrook Bank has completed a £2.98 million development exit loan for a nine-unit residential scheme in Wimbledon, with the transaction finalised in two and a half weeks from initial application. The development consisted of nine units comprising three flats and two mews houses.

title: First-time buyer hotspots emerge despite demand decline
summary:
First-time buyer demand fell 4% nationally in April, but West Oxfordshire saw demand surge 45% year-on-year. Regional markets are defying the national trend despite average monthly mortgage payments rising to £998.

title: Government announces building safety reforms after Grenfell
summary:
The Government has outlined new measures aimed at preventing a repeat of the Grenfell Tower disaster, including reforms to the building control sector and restrictions on engagement with companies implicated in the tragedy. The announcement follows plans to introduce a Remediation Bill designed to accelerate the removal of unsafe cladding from residential buildings.

title: NRLA and Lettings Industry Council announce merger
summary:
The National Residential Landlords Association has announced it will merge with The Lettings Industry Council, creating a unified body to represent landlords and letting agents across England and Wales. The merger comes weeks after the introduction of the Renters' Rights Act.

title: Self-employed estate agents show higher completion rates
summary:
Self-employed estate agents are achieving higher sale completion rates and faster transaction times than traditionally employed agents, according to new data from property analytics firm TwentyEA. The analysis found that self-employed agents had a 65.2% likelihood of completing a sale compared to 53.1% for traditionally employed agents.

title: UK inflation falls to 2.8% as mortgage rate cuts accelerate
summary:
UK inflation fell to 2.8% in April from 3.3% in March, prompting major lenders to reduce mortgage rates as market expectations grow for Bank of England rate cuts. Economists warn the decline may prove temporary due to rising oil prices and expected energy cost increases.

title: Goodlord partners with Reposit for deposit alternatives
summary:
Property technology firm Goodlord has announced Reposit as its sole partner for deposit replacement products, as the rental sector continues to adopt alternatives to traditional cash deposits. Under the agreement, Reposit will be the only integrated tenancy security solution on the Goodlord platform.

title: Thinktank proposes property wealth tax for London housing
summary:
The Centre for London has proposed replacing stamp duty and council tax with an annual property wealth tax to address the capital's housing challenges. The thinktank estimates the proportional property tax system could fund 106,000 social and affordable homes over the next decade while encouraging downsizing and helping renters save for deposits.
